role: Independent complete Theme B content and visual reviewer; separate from the Theme B author
author: chemistry_structure
scope: All 160 complete question-and-mark-scheme pairs, all 38 MCQ choices and rationales, all 12 SVG fields and the one supplied raster illustration. No sampling.
checks: Required biological knowledge independently compared with the corrected official guide and verified local blueprint, including shared versus additional HL scope.
Every prompt, option and marking point read. Distinct credits, relevant accepted reasoning, per-part marks and total allocations checked.
All schema, sequential identifiers, MCQ answer privacy and Markdown/KaTeX checks pass.
39 separate numerical or quantitative checks across28 questions independently recomputed from displayed inputs; the pressure-valve check evaluates every table row.
All constructed datasets are identified as constructed; named biological examples are separated from invented numerical datasets.
Error, confounding, replication, correlation/causation, limits of inference and model assumptions checked wherever relevant.
All 13 artwork fields inspected; anatomical locations, compartment boundaries, molecule/filament orientation, labels, graph scales and worked-answer placement agree with the respective tasks.
Seeded shuffled MCQ labels are balanced A10/B10/C9/D9; no repeated A-B-C-D allocation pattern.
Difficulty is assessed independently of the SL/AHL classification.

topicalReview.B1.1: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: carbon bonding, condensation/hydrolysis, alpha/beta glucose, storage and structural polysaccharides, recognition carbohydrates, triglycerides/phospholipids/steroids, fatty-acid packing, insulation and constructed energy/emulsion data. Reconciled molecular-link counts and carbohydrate/lipid fuel calculations.
topicalReview.B1.2: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: amino-acid and peptide structure, essentiality, denaturation, ordered sequence counts, dietary quantities, side-chain interactions, secondary/tertiary/quaternary structure and unfolding data. Detailed folding requirements correctly confined to AHL.
topicalReview.B2.1: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: diffusion/osmosis assumptions, channel and carrier function, pumps, membrane drawing, surface recognition, aquaporins, fluidity, cholesterol, vesicle transport, gating, sodium-potassium stoichiometry, cotransport and adhesion. Membrane placement is shared; extended mechanism requirements are AHL.
topicalReview.B2.2: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: course organelle convention, nuclear separation, compartment conditions, vacuoles/lysosomes, mitochondrial/chloroplast topology, nuclear pores, ribosome/ER/Golgi trafficking and clathrin. Required structural detail and trafficking content follow the shared/AHL division.
topicalReview.B2.3: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: potency and self-renewal, developmental gradients, niches, dimensions and surface-area-to-volume scaling, specialized exchange cells, microvilli, gametes and muscle-cell specializations. Extension surface-area model explicitly states its assumptions.
topicalReview.B3.1: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: exchange surfaces, ventilation mechanics, alveolar barrier, leaf pathways, lung-volume and stomatal calculations, potometer limitations, diffusion thickness, haemoglobin cooperation, Bohr effect and fetal affinity. Haemoglobin curve interpretation is AHL and percentage points are distinguished from percent changes.
topicalReview.B3.2: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: capillary/artery/vein structure, pulse, venous return, association versus causation, xylem/cohesion, dicot tissue arrangements, tissue fluid/lymph, double circulation, heart/septum/nodes, valve pressure states and root pressure. Heart detail and the extended transport mechanisms are AHL.
topicalReview.B3.3: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: locomotion, sliding filaments, titin, motor units, ATP and calcium roles, antagonistic action, static moments, joint movement, intercostals, marine-mammal adaptations and recruitment. All 16 correctly require AHL; myosin head polarity and fixed filament lengths checked visually.
topicalReview.B4.1: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: habitat/adaptation, limiting factors, tolerance, dune/mangrove/coral environments, biomes and named desert/rainforest plants, transects, factorial comparisons and common gardens. Constructed data remain identified and no unmeasured tolerance boundary or significance is inferred.
topicalReview.B4.2: Read all 16 prompts and schemes: niche, oxygen requirement, energy/carbon sources, saprotrophy/holozoic/mixotrophic nutrition, archaeal diversity, feeding adaptations and defences, light competition, realized niche and resource partitioning. Observational limitations and the separation of oxygen tolerance from nutrition are explicit.

closedFindings.resolution: Corrected the open-chain hydrolysis explanation: four separate chains have four fewer links than the total number of residues.
Specified the same non-dissociating solute and equal initial temperature/pressure for the predicted osmosis direction.
Closed syllabus breadth gaps through ABO recognition, aquaporins, septum/SAN/AV sequence, marine breathing and explicit oxygen-requirement categories.
Display precision is sufficient for the specified numerical answers.
Removed the answer from the general-amino-acid figure title/caption.
Attached and inspected the original labelled alveolar schematic used by the question.
Distinguished oxygen extracted and released to tissues from the ambiguous phrase total oxygen delivery.
Corrected opposite myosin-head directions across the centre of thick filaments.
Aligned the three-mark prompt with the exact three functional groups credited in its scheme.
Named black mangrove and independently verified salt glands and pneumatophores from the USDA fact sheet.
Replaced awkward auto-generated tick values with integer pH4–8 and20mg mass intervals.
Added a useful separate worked membrane diagram; corrected OH overlap and replaced a misleading ring icon with an explicitly labelled cholesterol position symbol.
Replaced cyclic answer positions with a seeded balanced shuffle and improved distractor wording before the final independent option review.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-017-question
figures.review: Neutral amino-acid convention, four alpha-carbon attachments and variable group X are clear; figure title/caption does not give the answer.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-022-solution
figures.review: The worked dipeptide correctly shows the carbonyl-to-nitrogen peptide linkage, terminal amino/carboxyl groups and distinct side groups.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-037-question
figures.review: Bilayer head/tail orientation, spanning channel and X/Y/Z pointers agree with the prompt and answer.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-037-solution
figures.review: Extracellular carbohydrate is attached to a membrane protein; the labelled cholesterol position symbol lies within one leaflet and its readable OH is near the heads. This is a positional schematic, not an inaccurate molecular skeleton.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-055-question
figures.review: Mitochondrial outer boundary, folded inner membrane/cristae and matrix pointers agree with the answer.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-057-question
figures.review: Chloroplast envelope, stroma and stacked thylakoid pointers agree with the answer.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-089-question
figures.review: Simplified leaf tissue arrangement places palisade tissue above spongy tissue and a stoma in the lower epidermal region; label pointers are unambiguous.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-101-question
figures.review: Thick vessel wall and lumen are clearly distinguished; caption correctly identifies the relative-thickness schematic.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-106-question
figures.review: Stem ring of vascular bundles and root central xylem with intervening phloem are correctly arranged and keyed.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-117-question
figures.review: Z discs, central thick filaments and anchored thin filaments are correct; the two halves of thick filaments have opposite myosin-head orientations.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-118-question
figures.review: Shortened Z-disc separation increases filament overlap without changing individual filament lengths; head polarity remains consistent.

figures.name: ib-bio-b-141-question
figures.review: All five points match the constructed table. The x-axis labels pH4–8 at integer intervals and the y-axis labels0–100mg in20mg intervals; there is no interpolation claim beyond supplied data.

At full resolution, A terminates on alveolar epithelium, B on capillary endothelium and C on an erythrocyte. The air-facing and blood-facing layers are distinct and closely apposed. Caption discloses an AI-assisted schematic rather than a micrograph.
